reproducible_features.notes: Exact mathematical equivalence for transaction sizing and round dollar amounts.
TransactionDT is elapsed seconds from a reference point, allowing diurnal and weekly cyclical feature extraction.
C-columns in IEEE-CIS quantify counting metrics (how many transactions were associated with the card/address). D-columns quantify timedelta from previous transactions.
train_identity.csv contains explicit browser, OS, and device metadata for a subset of transactions.
Frequency encodings learned strictly on historical training split.

non_reproducible_features.reason: IEEE-CIS is card-not-present merchant/e-commerce payment data. There are no distinct P2P 'sender' and 'receiver' counterparty IDs—only a purchaser card and merchant terminal.
Circular credit/fund flow (e.g., A -> B -> C -> A) requires directed P2P graph edges. In e-commerce card checkout, money flows unidirectionally from cardholder to merchant.
RingBreaker constructs an explicit directed multigraph of accounts. Fabricating synthetic P2P edges on IEEE-CIS would be academically dishonest and invalidate the benchmark.
Lockstep detection requires simultaneous micro-transactions across colluding sender-receiver nodes in a syndicate ring. IEEE-CIS has no ground-truth syndicate labels or multi-node P2P clusters.
Graph propagation algorithms require an interconnected node graph. Without counterparty graph edges, graph diffusion cannot be executed.
